arguments.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't take the battery out or cover the alarm. Yours is sealed, and a chirp every minute usually means it has reached the end of its life (it was fitted in 2019), so it needs replacing, not a new battery. Replacing it is our job, not yours. We've logged it as urgent and aim to get it replaced within 72 hours; we'll confirm a time with you. As we can't be sure it's only a fault, if the alarm ever sounds continuously, or you or anyone feel dizzy, sick, have headaches or smell gas: leave the flat, open doors, call the Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (or 999 if anyone is unwell), and tell us. We've also logged the noisy bathroom extractor fan as a routine job, to be dealt with within 14 days. Mare and Co Lettings

Hi Ben, the hallway CO alarm at Flat 9, 3 Amhurst Road (FireAngel CO-9X, fitted April 2019, sealed battery, 7-year life) is chirping, which points to end of life. As it's sealed, the tenant can't replace it, so replacement is your responsibility. We've logged it as urgent (JOB-101) and plan to arrange a like-for-like replacement alarm within 72 hours. We expect the cost to be well under your £300 limit; we'll tell you if that changes. We've also logged a routine noisy extractor fan job (JOB-102). Tenant has been given safety advice. Regards, Mare and Co Lettings

arguments.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't take the battery out or cover the alarm. Yours is sealed, and a chirp every minute usually means it has reached the end of its life (it was fitted in 2019), so it needs replacing, not a new battery. Replacing it is our job, not yours. We've logged it as urgent and aim to get it replaced within 72 hours; we'll confirm a time with you.
